title: Internet Governance Through Site Shutdowns: The Impact of Shutting Down Two Major Commercial Sex Advertising Sites
authors: Helen Shuxuan Zeng; Brett Danaher; Michael D. Smith
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Common shutdown date for all cities (Craigslist personals March 23, 2018; Backpage April 6, 2018; post from 2018-04).
eligible_reason: Continuous-intensity, single-date design. Table 2 (main.do lines 153-171): reghdfe <rate> after, a(cityid dm) cluster(cityid), with after = a x penetration, where penetration is the city's pre-shutdown ad volume on the two shut sites per 100,000 residents (continuous) and a marks months after the common shutdown. Event-study figures interact penetration with month dummies. No binary treatment with unit-specific adoption dates. In addition the data are not shipped (IBM TA Hub and Marinus Analytics data under NDA; package has only main.do and smcl logs).
design_notes: City-month panel (cities with pop >= 100,000), outcomes per 100k: ads on other/offshore/domestic sites, trafficking cases, prostitution arrests, female homicides, rape. Table 2: static continuous-intensity DiD with city and month FE; Figures 3-7: penetration x month leads/lags; Tables A2-A6 robustness.
data_access_note: Ad-volume and trafficking data under NDA; available to researchers who sign an equivalent NDA (readme.pdf).
screener_notes: Screened from package only (abstract from data/frame/mnsc.jsonl: 'generalized difference-in-differences model by exploiting cross-city variation in the preshutdown usage').
